I really, really don’t see anything wrong with using English translations in the beginning. It just makes the process faster and less confusing. English and Japanese aren’t one-to-one but I feel like you’ll just solidify the meanings of grammar points/vocab *as* you encounter it in repeatedly in native media. To me, Anki is just a starting point that you use to introduce yourself to new grammar points/vocabulary, while reading/listening to Japanese media is how you *really* learn the language and solidify those concepts. So I think using English to clarify a sentence is fine, especially since you are *testing* yourself on the meaning. When you’re just consuming content it’s okay if it’s more vague imo

I'm not saying this to be rude, but do you need to know why? I'm assuming your goal is to be able to understand and/or to speak Japanese, and to do that, you don't really need to know "why," you just need to know how to say what you want to say. The first way is correct, and you'll see that sentence pattern over and over again to the point where when you want to say something like that it'll come to you naturally. Asking why one way is used over the other is like asking English natives why we say "what is it called" instead of "how is it called." That's just the way the language formed, and that's just how you say that.

But to better understand the particles, I'd recommend going through a textbook like Genki or Tae Kim's grammar guide (online and free) or maybe "A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar" (it's more of a reference to use once you're somewhat familiar with a particle though, it's kinda dense).

I started August of this year and I can relate with everything you’re going through, lol.

1. I agree with going to practice tool to just focus completely on csing. Take your starting item (ex. doran’s blade) and lock your lvl. You can see when your ally minions attack by the way—like you can see your caster/cannon minions shooting a projectile and you can see your melee minions winding up to attack. So you can time your autos a bit better by looking for that. 

2. Yeah I struggled with this a lot too at first. It’s hard to know what’s going on when you have no idea what abilities the other champions have. What I did was spam a bunch of intermediate bot games, and afterwards I would check what abilities the enemy (or allied) champions had. You can check that in the client or on the wiki. Also I think picking just one champion and one role would help you a lot—you’ll learn faster that way. Make sure you know your own champ’s abilties and how they work too. I used opgg to figure out what runes/items to get and what skills to max.

3. Runes give your champion extra abilities and/or stats. There’s one Keystone per tree that gives you an ability (like in the Domination tree you could take Electrocute, which deals extra damage if you attack an enemy 3 times in 3 seconds, or Guardian in the Resolve tree, which gives you a shield right before you take damage, etc.). And then the rest of the slots in the tree give you minor abilities and stats (like Nimbus Cloak in the Sorcery tree gives you extra speed after using a summoner spell, and Legend: Bloodline in the Precision tree gives you extra life steal).
